outcome: Pregnancy complications (cervical infection, spontaneous abortion, premature birth - background)
Complications (minor cervical laceration, postpartum hemorrhage, retained placenta)
cohort: Eight women with advanced uterine prolapse (mean age 30.3 years, 7 with POPQ stage >= 3) diagnosed during pregnancy were included from a single university-affiliated hospital.
finding: Conservative management with vaginal pessary insertion for pelvic organ prolapse in pregnancy was tolerable, provided symptomatic relief, and minimized pregnancy complications.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was found to be feasible for most women and associated with low complication rates.
